summary: Thomas de Bruijn is an Indologist who held posts at Leiden University (attested 1998-1999) and the International Institute for Asian Studies (attested 1998).

Thomé H. Fang (1899-1977) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Nanking, under John Dewey, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925-1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948-1973).

Thubten Chodron (born 1950) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama and Thubten Yeshe. She founded Sravasti Abbey, serving as its abbess.

Thubten Jigme Norbu (1922-2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima, served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965-1992).

Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. As a teacher, his students included the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Thubten Samphel (1956-2022) was a Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University. He later held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thubten Yeshe (1935-1984) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Zong Rinpoche. He co-founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977-1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946-2023) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Yeshe and the 14th Dalai Lama. He co-founded Kopan Monastery, FPMT, and Maitripa College, serving as FPMT's spiritual director.

Thupten Jinpa (born 1958) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Zongkar Choede, Ganden Shartse, and Cambridge. He founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics and held posts at Ganden Shartse, Girton College, and Stanford University.
Thupten Tsering works in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology, holding posts at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China and Tibet University.
Thushini S. Jayawardena works in religious studies and other fields. She studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka and earned a PhD from Auckland University of Technology by 2017.

Théodore Pavie (1811-1896) was an Indologist and Sinologist. He studied at Lycée David d'Angers and under Eugène Burnouf and Garcin de Tassy. He later succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at Collège de France (1852-1857) and taught at the Catholic University of the West.

Thích Minh Châu (1918-2012) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1957-1964) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (1964-1975).
Thích Thiện Châu (1931-1998) was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who pursued his studies at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967-1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1971-1977).

Tianshu Zhu works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Northwest University and under John C. Huntington at Ohio State University (PhD 2007). Her career includes posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State, Korea University, and University of Macau (2007).

Tilak Kariyawasam (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937-2012) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Heintel and Erich Frauwallner, and became a professor at Leiden University in 1974, succeeding David Seyfort Ruegg.

Timothy C. Cahill is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at the University of Iowa (attested 1995), University of Pennsylvania (attested 1997), Loyola University Chicago (attested 2012), and Loyola University New Orleans (attested 2010, 2019-2023).

Timothy Dubber is an Indology and history/archaeology researcher who studied at UNSW Canberra, the University of Edinburgh, and Australian National University. He is scheduled as an ANU PhD candidate (2025) and Adjunct Fellow at UNSW (2026).

Timothy Hugh Barrett (born 1947) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University, later teaching at Cambridge (attested 1981) and becoming Professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.
